name: The General's Response
summary: General Marcus Jonathan sends word to Lakeshire while Redridge waits for aid. His dispatch acknowledges Magistrate Solomon's plea against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, but offers no immediate reinforcements from Stormwind.

sections.title: A Diplomatic Standoff
sections.body: Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Stormwind City for troops to defend Redridge from the gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands. General Marcus Jonathan replies that the plea has been forwarded to the throne, but no soldiers are being sent now. He orders the letter returned to Lakeshire. Solomon is left troubled by Stormwind's delay and suspicious that something is wrong with its leaders.

faq.q: What is written in The General's Response?
faq.answer: General Marcus Jonathan mourns the dead and says he will make the King aware of Lakeshire's plight. He hopes to bring reinforcements and confides that His Majesty has been scarce and acting oddly.

faq.q: Why can't General Marcus Jonathan send troops to Lakeshire?
faq.answer: General Jonathan awaits the King's response before promising reinforcements. In confidence, he tells Solomon that His Majesty has been scarce and acting oddly.

faq.q: How does Magistrate Solomon react to the letter?
faq.answer: Magistrate Solomon is deeply unsettled by the dispatch. Stormwind's slowness makes no sense to him while Lakeshire faces such danger, and he fears the neglect points to worse trouble in the kingdom.

angles.text: Stormwind's response shows the strain on the Grand Alliance. Lakeshire bleeds while the court appears strangely unresponsive to its plight.
For humans of the southern kingdoms, the delayed reply shows the growing rift between people fighting for survival in the provinces and the secluded nobility in Stormwind Keep.
